```{r dataset-overview}
    "Pancreatic islets",
    "133 (ND=18, IGT=41, T3cD=35, T2D=39)",
    "98",
    "Normoglycaemic (ND, n=18), Impaired Glucose Tolerant (IGT, n=41), Type 2 Diabetic (T2D, n=39)",
    "58,336",
```

# 2. Differential Expression Analysis

## 2.1 Summary of Significant Differentially Expressed Genes

```{r de-summary}
de_summary <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("T2D vs ND", "IGT vs ND", "T2D vs IGT"),
  Total_DEGs = c(604, 193, 245),
  Upregulated = c("563", "189", "210"),
  Downregulated = c("41", "4", "35"),
  FDR_Threshold = c("< 0.05", "< 0.05", "< 0.05"),
  Method = c("DESeq2 Wald test (BH)", "DESeq2 Wald test (BH)", "DESeq2 Wald test (BH)")
)

kable(de_summary,
      col.names = c("Comparison", "Total DEGs", "Upregulated",
                    "Downregulated", "FDR Threshold", "Correction Method"),
      caption = "Table 2. Summary of differentially expressed genes across three pairwise comparisons. DEGs = differentially expressed genes; BH = Benjamini-Hochberg.",
      align = c("l","c","c","c","c","l"))
```

## 2.1b Covariate-Adjusted Sensitivity Analysis

```{r de-covariate-overlap}
covariate_overlap <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("T2D vs ND", "IGT vs ND", "T2D vs IGT"),
  Primary_DEGs = c(604, 193, 245),
  Covariate_Adjusted_DEGs = c(615, 180, 204),
  Shared = c(452, 123, 189),
  Lost = c(152, 70, 56),
  Gained = c(163, 57, 15),
  Pct_Survived = c("74.8%", "63.7%", "77.1%")
)

kable(covariate_overlap,
      col.names = c("Comparison", "Primary DEGs", "Covariate-Adjusted DEGs",
                    "Shared", "Lost", "Gained", "% of Primary Surviving"),
      caption = "Table 2b. DEG overlap between the primary (design = ~status) and covariate-adjusted (design = ~age + bmi + status) DESeq2 models. Age (ANOVA p=0.0077) and BMI (p=0.0146) differed significantly across ND/IGT/T2D groups; the majority of the primary DEG list survives adjustment, confirming it is not primarily attributable to this confound. Of the 15 named hub/DE genes discussed in Chapter 3, 14 survive adjustment — the exception is PLA2G2A (brown module).",
      align = c("l","c","c","c","c","c","c"))
```

```{r de-top10}
                   "CLTRN","PIGA","GABRA2","RASGRP1"),
  Base_Mean = c(469.95, 22.03, 102.35, 625.24, 657.35,

  log2FC = c(-1.68, 5.79, 1.66, -1.76, 2.97,

      align = c("l","l","r","r","r","c"),
      digits = 2)
```

# 4. WGCNA Co-expression Network

## 4.1 Network Construction Parameters

```{r wgcna-params}

  Parameter = c(

    "Scale-free topology fit (R²)",
    "Network type",
    "Correlation method",
    "Minimum module size",
    "Module merge threshold (cut height)",
    "Samples retained",

    "Grey (unassigned) module size"
  ),
  Value = c(
    "8",
    "0.851",
    "Signed",
    "Biweight midcorrelation (bicor)",
    "30 genes",
    "0.25 (eigengene correlation > 0.75)",
    "98",
    "20,042",
    "30 (including grey)",
    "5,473 genes"
  ),
  Justification = c(
    "Lowest power achieving R² ≥ 0.80 (Zhang & Horvath, 2005)",
    "Within recommended 0.80–0.90 range",
```

# 5. Functional Enrichment Analysis

## 5.1 GO Biological Process Enrichment — T2D vs ND (Top Terms)

```{r go-de}
go_de <- data.frame(
  GO_ID = c("GO:0006956","GO:0002250","GO:0006959",
             "GO:0002443","GO:0002449","GO:0002697","GO:0002683"),
  Description = c("Complement activation",
                   "Adaptive immune response",
                   "Humoral immune response",
                   "Leukocyte mediated immunity",
                   "Lymphocyte mediated immunity",
                   "Regulation of immune effector process",
                   "Negative regulation of immune system process"),
  Gene_Ratio = c("19/459","65/459","38/459",
                  "50/459","40/459","46/459","56/459"),
  Rich_Factor = c(0.475,0.173,0.226,0.161,0.171,0.148,0.123),
  Significance = c("***","***","***","***","***","***","***")
)

kable(go_de,
      col.names = c("GO ID","Description","Gene Ratio",
                    "Rich Factor","Significance"),
      caption = "Table 8. Top Gene Ontology Biological Process terms enriched among differentially expressed genes in T2D versus ND. Gene Ratio = DEGs annotated to term / total DEGs with GO annotation. Rich Factor = Gene Ratio / Background Ratio. *** = FDR < 0.001.",
      align = c("l","l","c","r","c"),
      digits = 3)
```

# 6. Machine Learning Classification

## 6.1 Binary Classification Performance — T2D vs ND

```{r ml-binary}
ml_binary <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Random Forest","Logistic Regression","SVM (RBF kernel)","XGBoost"),
  AUC_Mean = c(0.992, 0.992, 0.992, 0.992),
  AUC_SD = c(0.017, 0.017, 0.017, 0.017),
  BACC_Mean = c(0.954, 0.988, 0.942, 0.929),
  BACC_SD = c(0.092, 0.025, 0.089, 0.093),
  Permutation_p = c("0.010","—","—","—")
)

kable(ml_binary,
      col.names = c("Model","AUC (mean)","AUC (SD)",
                    "Balanced Accuracy (mean)","Balanced Accuracy (SD)",
                    "Permutation p-value"),
      caption = "Table 11. Five-fold stratified cross-validation performance of binary classifiers (T2D vs ND) using WGCNA hub gene expression features. AUC = area under the ROC curve. Balanced Accuracy accounts for class imbalance. Permutation test: 100 permutations; p = 0.010 confirms the Random Forest result is not attributable to chance. NOTE: hub-gene features were selected using module-trait correlation across all 98 samples prior to this cross-validation, which likely inflates these figures — see Table 11b for a leakage-free re-estimate.",
      align = c("l","c","c","c","c","c"))
```

## 6.1b Leakage-Free Nested Validation — T2D vs ND

```{r ml-nested}
ml_nested <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Random Forest","Logistic Regression","SVM (RBF kernel)"),
  Standard_CV_AUC = c(0.992, 0.992, 0.992),
  Nested_Holdout_AUC_Mean = c(0.938, 0.944, 0.938),
  Nested_Holdout_AUC_SD = c(0.086, 0.064, 0.058),
  Nested_Holdout_AUC_Range = c("0.844-1.000", "0.875-1.000", "0.844-1.000")
)

kable(ml_nested,
      col.names = c("Model","Standard CV AUC","Nested held-out AUC (mean)",
                    "Nested held-out AUC (SD)","Range across 5 splits"),
      caption = "Table 11b. Leakage-free nested validation: WGCNA modules, hub-gene ranking, and differential expression evidence were re-derived from a training-only subset (78 of 98 samples) for five independent stratified splits, with each classifier evaluated exactly once on the untouched 20-sample held-out set per split (n=12 T2D/ND held-out samples per split). The ~5-percentage-point drop from standard CV confirms the standard estimate was optimistic due to feature-selection circularity, while the held-out AUC remaining well above chance confirms the underlying hub-gene signal is genuinely predictive rather than a leakage artefact.",
      align = c("l","c","c","c","c"))
```

## 6.2 Three-Class Classification Performance — ND / IGT / T2D

```{r ml-multiclass}
ml_multi <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Random Forest (standard CV)", "Random Forest (leakage-free nested, n=5 splits)"),
  BACC_Mean = c(0.689, 0.708),
  BACC_SD = c(0.129, 0.098),
  Interpretation = c(
    "Moderate performance; IGT-T2D boundary is biologically ambiguous",
    "Near-identical to standard CV — confirms IGT difficulty is intrinsic, not a leakage artefact"
  )
)

kable(ml_multi,
      col.names = c("Model","Balanced Accuracy (mean)",
                    "Balanced Accuracy (SD)","Interpretation"),
      caption = "Table 12. Three-class (ND / IGT / T2D) cross-validation performance, standard vs leakage-free nested estimation. Lower balanced accuracy compared to binary classification reflects the biological continuity between IGT and T2D, which reduces class separability.",
      align = c("l","c","c","l"))
```
